Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Greenville-Spartanburg SC
622 PM EST Sun Nov 22 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Aviation discussion was updated to reflect the 00Z TAFs.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
1. On the Monday morning commute, drive carefully and be prepared
to encounter areas of fog. Temperatures trend warmer for Monday
and then cooler for Tuesday.
2. Rain becomes likely Wednesday, and may last into Thanksgiving
Day. Dry weather and near-normal temperatures at the end of
the week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Key message 1: On the Monday morning commute, drive carefully and be 
prepared to encounter areas of fog. Temperatures trend warmer for 
Monday and then cooler for Tuesday.

Low-level winds back to northerly and then westerly through Monday 
morning, but with speeds light enough that wedge erosion is expected 
to occur only slowly. High boundary layer RH persists and as often 
occurs with a nocturnal wedge erosion process, fog appears likely to 
become widespread and visibilities to lower toward dawn. While we 
are not yet confident enough to say dense fog will be widespread, it 
is advisable for drivers to watch out for locally dense fog during 
the Monday morning commute, slow down, and leave extra space between 
vehicles.

Fog and cloud cover should dissipate over the foothills and
Piedmont during the morning. Northwest winds pick up as a cold
front approaches from the Tennessee Valley, with upslope clouds
and scattered showers persisting much of the day along the NC/TN
border. CAA occurs early enough there, that combined with the
cloud cover temps remain similar to today's values; for valley
locations away from the border and across the foothills/Piedmont,
temperatures trend warmer. Expect afternoon maxes in the 70s in most
of the Piedmont, some 10 degrees above normal. A few sprinkles or
light showers could develop in the Piedmont during the afternoon
with a shallow unstable layer ahead of the front.

The cooler air brings temps back to near normal for the mountains 
Monday night into Tuesday morning. Max temps Tuesday slightly below 
normal as strong continental high pressure builds in from the 
Midwest and subsequently migrates to the northeast CONUS. Wednesday 
morning mins expected to be a tad below normal.


Key message 2: Rain becomes likely Wednesday, and may last into
Thanksgiving Day. Dry weather and near-normal temperatures at the
end of the week.

Classical CAD setup looks to be in place Wednesday morning with
global models agreeing on a very dry 1040+ mb surface high centered
over New England, as the early-week cold front stalls over north
Florida. Meanwhile a deep shortwave is shown to become negatively
tilted over the lower Mississippi Valley, which should promote
warm upglide north of the stalled front and over the CAD wedge,
leading to increasing precip chances for our CWA over the course of
Wednesday. A cold start, followed by thickening clouds and diabatic
cooling from developing precip, suggest Wednesday as the coolest
day of the forecast period, with max temps mainly in the upper 40s
to lower 50s, perhaps even colder if precip starts earlier than
currently expected. As moistening occurs and temps and wet-bulb
temps (Tw) quickly rise well above freezing, it presently looks
unlikely precip will start as anything but rain that day, except
in very high elevations of the mountains (mainly above 6000 ft)
where Tw profiles support brief snow or perhaps sleet at onset, if
precip begins early enough. Minimal accumulation is expected even
at those high elevations. Even given the wedge, LREF joint probs
of surface Tw below 32 and measurable precip are less than 10%
Wednesday morning. The more likely scenario is that precipitation
does not begin until later in the day when surface temps have
warmed enough for only rain at the surface.

By late Wednesday evening or early Thursday (Thanksgiving) morning
cyclogenesis should be underway along the stalled front, driving
a strong easterly LLJ over our CWA promoting even stronger upglide
and moisture flux, so forecast PoPs peak at that time, greater than
75% for virtually the whole CWA. The incipient low still looks most
likely to track northward toward the Outer Banks; 22/06z operational
GFS is a western outlier compared to global deterministic models
and the majority of ensemble members. Nevertheless, on account
of the LLJ, GFS/ECMWF ensemble PWATs peak at 175-200% of normal
Wednesday night, and a period of heavy rain would appear likely
around that time. That said, per global ensembles, probabilities of
even 1" in 6 hours or 2" in 24 hours are both low, although those
probabilities very well may increase as the event moves into the
range of higher resolution models, even if the general setup remains
the same. Takeaway for now is that the risk of flooding still looks
low for the event, but it bears watching. Temps Wed night certainly
would be chilly but most likely comfortably above freezing with
a strong warm nose still aloft, so only rain is expected. The
CAD should erode Thanksgiving Day as the trough/low pass, and as
NW winds develop at the surface. Precip gradually diminishes in
coverage from SW to NE. Max temps warm back to near normal in the
Piedmont and perhaps just below normal in the mountains. As the
system pulls away, can't rule out some light precip along the NC/TN
border Thursday night, and as temps fall again some of that precip
could transition to light snow or rime ice, but as moisture becomes
very shallow accumulation is unlikely to be of appreciable impact.

The remainder of the period looks dry with temperatures near
normal. There are hints from some guidance that another passing
shortwave could induce light precip Saturday or early Sunday,
but such a shortwave would have very little moisture to work with,
so we keep PoPs below slight-chance in that timeframe.

&&

.AVIATION /00Z MONDAY THROUGH FRIDAY/...
At KCLT and elsewhere: A mix of MVFR/IFR to start this TAF period, 
with additional restrictions anticipated overnight. BR/FG could 
create IFR/LIFR conditions at most terminals as winds become lighter 
to calm. KCLT could have 2SM vsby while elsewhere 1-2SM likely 
between 09z-14z. Conditions should slowly improve late Monday 
morning as vsby improves to VFR and cigs SCT. Winds remain N/NE and 
light on Monday.

Outlook: Drier conditions linger through Tuesday before widespread 
rain chances and periodic restrictions return Wednesday and into 
Thursday. Drier and mostly VFR conditions should return by Friday.
